row.evidence: Sugar's help centre documents SCIM for SugarIdentity-enabled instances with Okta, OneLogin and Azure, but neither the pricing page (Standard+ $68, Advanced+ $98, Premier+ $155) nor the docs name the plan that includes SugarIdentity/SCIM.
row.notes: SugarCRM rebranded as SugarAI (sugarai.com). SCIM 2.0 runs through SugarIdentity: create, update, deactivate (status Inactive, frees the licence seat) and delete; no group push or custom attributes. Okta and OneLogin need SAML configured first; Azure does not. SSO is documented as not supported on Sugar Sell Essentials, a tier no longer on the pricing page; the pricing page lists no SSO or SCIM by tier, so the status stays unknown under rule 1a. REST API (OAuth2) has /Users endpoints; plan availability not stated.

auth.token_source: SugarIdentity > SCIM Settings > Create Client (Server URL, Username, Password, Bearer Token)
auth.notes: OneLogin and Azure use the Bearer Token; the Okta app uses the generated Username and Password.

endpoints.notes: Group push is not supported; the Azure guide disables group provisioning. No SCIM endpoint list is published.

operations.notes: Update is documented ('Update User'), but whether it uses PUT or PATCH is not stated.

deprovision.data_retained: Status set to Inactive; the user can no longer log in but historical data remains in SugarCRM; records can be reassigned. A SCIM delete (OneLogin/Azure) deletes the SugarIdentity user and the corresponding user and employee records.

attributes.notes: From SugarIdentity's OneLogin SCIM JSON template; no full schema reference is published.

roles.how: Teams and roles are assigned manually in Sugar after the SCIM user is created.

limitations.text: Group push and password sync are not supported; custom attributes are not supported.
Okta's SugarIdentity app supports create, update and deactivate only (no delete).
Requires SugarIdentity; Okta and OneLogin also require SAML to be configured first.

scim.notes: SCIM requires a SugarIdentity-enabled instance (SugarCloud, or on-site after activation). SAML must be configured first for Okta and OneLogin, but not for Azure/Entra. The Server URL is generated per tenant in SugarIdentity > SCIM Settings; no URL pattern is documented.

capabilities.notes: Users is a regular Sugar module, so the generic /<module> create and update endpoints apply; team/role relationships via /Users/:record/link. On SugarIdentity-enabled instances user identity fields are managed in SugarIdentity.

endpoints.purpose: Link a user to an existing record (e.g. team, role)
List user records for IdM migration (includes password hashes)
Create a record (generic module endpoint, applies to Users)
Update a record (generic module endpoint, applies to Users)

okta.notes: OIN app 'SugarCRM (SugarIdentity)' ticks SCIM, Create, Update and Deactivate (SAML is not ticked on the listing); Sugar requires SAML to be configured separately before SCIM.

entra.notes: Gallery app 'Sugar CRM' is SSO only; Sugar's SCIM guide uses a non-gallery 'Create your own application' with the generic SCIM endpoint.

onelogin.notes: Sugar's guide uses OneLogin's generic 'SCIM Provisioner with SAML (SCIM v2)' app, not a dedicated catalogue app.

fallbacks.other_sync: LDAP authentication with auto-create on first login

searched: SugarIdentity guide, user management and external authentication docs
Sugar Developer Guide 26.1 REST API endpoints
open_questions: Which Sugar Sell / Serve tiers include SugarIdentity SAML SSO and SCIM is not stated on the pricing page or in the docs (only that SSO is not supported on Sugar Sell Essentials).
SCIM endpoint list, filtering, pagination, PUT vs PATCH, token expiry and rate limits are not documented.
Whether SCIM deactivation ends active sessions is not documented.
Whether REST API access differs by tier is not stated.
Pricing page tabs for Market, Serve and Enterprise did not render in the static fetch; Sugar Sell prices only.
Google Workspace and JumpCloud catalogue apps not checked/found.
